cards.explanation: The message claims that the Day of the Lord has already come. Paul asks the brothers not to be easily disconcerted or alarmed by any spirit or message or letter seeming to be from him and his team, alleging that the Day of the Lord has already come (2 Thessalonians 2:2). A letter with a famous name at the bottom isn't always from that person, friends.

The answer is False. Paul warns the brothers about any spirit or message or letter alleging that the Day of the Lord has already come (2 Thessalonians 2:2), and he tells them not to be deceived. He says "…it will not come until the rebellion occurs and the man of lawlessness—the son of destruction—is revealed." (2 Thessalonians 2:3) The warning is the whole point of his letter here.

The answer is God, and he'll go as high as it gets. He will "…exalt himself above every so-called god or object of worship." proclaiming himself to be God (2 Thessalonians 2:4). That's the biggest claim a person could make, and it's a false one. Paul wants the brothers to know it ahead of time.

The answer is in the temple of God. Paul says, "So he will seat himself in the temple of God, proclaiming himself to be God." (2 Thessalonians 2:4) He doesn't pick some random spot. He sits down right where God is worshiped.

The answer is that Paul told them in person. Paul asks, "Do you not remember that I told you these things while I was still with you?" (2 Thessalonians 2:5) He's reminding them, not teaching them fresh. They heard it from him when he was with them.

The answer is until he is taken out of the way. Paul says, "…the one who now restrains it will continue until he is taken out of the way." (2 Thessalonians 2:7) The text doesn't say more about who he is or how he's removed. So I'll leave it open, friends, right where the text leaves it.

The answer is True. Paul says the Lord Jesus will slay the lawless one "…with the breath of His mouth…" and annihilate him "…by the majesty of His arrival." (2 Thessalonians 2:8) There's no battle of equals here. Jesus wins, plain and simple.

The word is truth, friends. Paul says they perish "…because they refused the love of the truth that would have saved them." (2 Thessalonians 2:10) Refusing the love of the truth is the reason he gives.

The answer is that they delighted in wickedness. Paul says judgment comes upon "…all who have disbelieved the truth and delighted in wickedness." (2 Thessalonians 2:12) The two go together in his words.

The answer is from the beginning. Paul says, "…God chose you from the beginning to be saved by the sanctification of the Spirit and by faith in the truth." (2 Thessalonians 2:13) Their salvation was no last-minute thing. God had it in mind from the beginning.

The answer is True. Paul says that God chose them "…to be saved by the sanctification of the Spirit and by faith in the truth." (2 Thessalonians 2:13) That's a nice contrast with those who refused the love of the truth (2 Thessalonians 2:10). The Thessalonians are in the group who believed.

The answer is to share in the glory of Jesus Christ. Paul says God called them through the gospel "…so that you may share in the glory of our Lord Jesus Christ." (2 Thessalonians 2:14) The gospel is how the call reached them, and the glory is what it leads to.

The word is firm. Paul says, "…stand firm and cling to the traditions we taught you, whether by speech or by letter." (2 Thessalonians 2:15) After all those warnings, he gives them something to do. Plant your feet, friends, and hold on.

The answer is False. Paul says, "…cling to the traditions we taught you, whether by speech or by letter." (2 Thessalonians 2:15) So the teaching came by speech and by letter, not only one of them. Paul wants them to stand firm and cling to it either way.

The answer is eternal comfort and good hope. Paul points to God our Father, "…who by grace has loved us and given us eternal comfort and good hope…" (2 Thessalonians 2:16) Those are the two gifts he names. The comfort is eternal and the hope is good.
